label: Target
definition: The answer is about whether the vendor reached the right people with the right message
include: who the vendor approaches; relevance of the message to the person or role; being the wrong audience
example: I've been treated as if I don't know what I'm doing

label: Access
definition: The answer is about getting in front of the decision-maker
include: how vendors make contact; persistence; referrals; being screened; getting a meeting
example: Rapid7 - Far too agressive on their marketing.

label: Agree
definition: The answer is about the meeting and the salesperson's conduct in it — whether the decision-maker agrees to explore further
include: preparation; listening; understanding the business; pitching; insight; professionalism in the meeting
exclude: the plan or business case (Vision, Case)

label: Vision
definition: The answer is about building a shared picture of the solution and the path to value
include: solution fit; seeing how value is delivered; material; involving others; who will execute
example: The ability to link a product that can be integrated in our specific IT environment.

label: Case
definition: The answer is about the business case: justification, risk, price, value for money, authority to buy
include: ROI; price; cost; risk; contract terms; approval
exclude: general product quality without a business-case claim

label: After the business case
definition: The answer is about the relationship once the vendor is chosen — delivery, service, account management, support over time
include: support; after-sales; follow-through on commitments; long-term account relationship; product performance in use
exclude: the selling conversation before a decision (earlier gates)
example: Account Manager-stays close to OUR business
source: M10; Scott 2026-10-29 (contract is terminal; relationship accounts); example Q24-R020

label: No single gate
definition: The answer is about the vendor or salesperson in general, with no stage implied
include: general traits (honest, professional) not tied to a stage
exclude: an answer that names a stage

label: Reliability
definition: Ability to perform the promised service dependably and accurately
include: keeps commitments; delivers; does what they say; consistent quality
example: what they deliver does what they say it does
source: M6 Parasuraman et al. 1988; example Q22-R026

label: Responsiveness
definition: Willingness to help and provide prompt service
include: quick reply; available; reacts fast; follows up

label: Assurance
definition: Knowledge and courtesy, and the ability to inspire trust and confidence
include: expertise; competence; credibility; trust; honesty; professionalism

label: Empathy
definition: Caring, individualised attention to the customer
include: understands my business or needs; listens; tailored; partnership; personal relationship

label: Tangibles
definition: Physical and presented evidence — materials, presentations, appearance, the product itself as seen
include: presentations; materials; demos; product features as shown
exclude: the conduct of the person (other dimensions)

label: No SERVQUAL dimension
definition: The answer expresses none of the five dimensions
include: price; brand; product category only

label: Attribute
definition: A concrete or abstract property of the vendor, salesperson or product
include: 'knowledgeable', 'responsive', 'good product', 'pushy'

label: Consequence
definition: What the property does for (or to) the decision-maker or the company
include: 'saves us time', 'issues get resolved', 'wastes my time'
example: Consultant-easy to contact n solve issues!

label: Value
definition: The end the decision-maker cares about — personal or organisational
include: 'trust', 'success of the initiative', 'peace of mind', 'partnership', 'our business grows'
example: how they can best help me and the team achieve the required results

label: The vendor organisation
definition: Credit or blame placed on the company as a whole
include: company culture, policy, offering, reputation
example: established companies,have resources we can use

label: The salesperson or sales team
definition: Credit or blame placed on the people who sell or manage the account
include: rep, account manager, sales team, consultant behaviour
example: Account Manager-stays close to OUR business

label: The product or service
definition: Credit or blame placed on what is sold
include: quality, features, price of the offering

label: The decision-maker's own company
definition: Credit or blame placed on the respondent's own organisation or self
include: 'we did not have the capability', 'our processes'

label: No attribution
definition: No one is credited or blamed
include: names only; general statements

label: Positive
definition: The answer expresses approval
include: praise; 'good', 'best', 'responsive'

label: Negative
definition: The answer expresses disapproval
include: criticism; 'pushy', 'worthless', 'unprepared'

label: Mixed
definition: The answer expresses both
include: 'good product but pushy'

label: Neutral
definition: No evaluation
include: a role or names only; a description

label: Non-answer
definition: No substantive content
include: 'none', 'n/a', 'don't know', refusals

label: Names only
definition: Only vendor names, no reason or description
include: 'Microsoft, Xerox, HP'

label: Role only
definition: Only a contact role or channel, no reason (Q24, Q25)
include: 'account manager', 'consultant', 'e-mail'

label: Unintelligible
definition: Text that cannot be read as an answer
include: 'aze', 'A B C', keyboard strings

label: Refers to another answer
definition: Points to an earlier answer without content
include: 'same answer', 'see previous response'

label: Off topic
definition: A deliberate joke or unrelated text
include: 'Pickles Onions Mustard'
example: Anchovies are ALWAYS a bad choice.

label: A value, not an evaluation
definition: An amount or factual description with nothing to code (Q20_2 amounts, S4 role descriptions)
include: '250000', 'Desktop Support'

label: Knows my business
definition: The salesperson or vendor understands the decision-maker's business, industry, company or needs. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: knows our business, industry, company, needs, environment
example: The ability to understand our business need
source: M4 seed; Q8_3/Q8_5; lexicon L11; example Q21-R045

label: Listens
definition: Listens to what the decision-maker wants rather than talking. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: listens; asks questions; hears us out

label: Responsive
definition: Replies and acts promptly; available when needed. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: quick response; available; reacts; follows up promptly
example: Dell - they are unresponsive and hard to pin down
source: M4 seed; SERVQUAL responsiveness; example Q23-R276

label: Knows the product
definition: Knowledge of their own products, services or technology. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: product knowledge; technical expertise; competence in their offering
example: IBM, SAP and Oracle for the expertise.

label: Prepared
definition: Comes prepared to the meeting. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: prepared; did their homework; organised
example: Preparedness and understanding of our company and our problems

label: Honest and trustworthy
definition: Honest, transparent, keeps their word; can be trusted. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: honest; trustworthy; transparent; integrity
example: Accenture as they cannot be trusted for what they say

label: Puts my needs before their sale
definition: Serves the decision-maker's interest rather than the vendor's sale; − : pushy, oversells, only wants the sale. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: doesn't oversell; genuinely cares; − : pushy, aggressive, hard sell, quick deal for them
example: Xerox know my needs and don't oversell
source: M2/M4 (deductive (renamed from B-PUSHY so every behaviour code is a dimension with + and −)); example Q22-R292

label: Brings insight and ideas
definition: Brings new ideas, innovation, strategic perspective or the big picture. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: innovative; insight; strategic direction; big picture; − : no strategy, not strategic, loses the bigger picture
example: Those that are innovators vs a "me too"

label: Brings the vendor's organisation
definition: Can mobilise the vendor's own people, specialists and resources for the customer. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: has clout; knows the bench and who can help; direct access to specialists; resources we can use; − : lacks resources, no direct sales
example: Account manager - have clout inside their organisations

label: Empowered to decide
definition: Has the authority to make decisions or commitments. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: can make decisions; empowered; can make commitments; − : no autonomy, not authorised
example: Executive: Can make decisions and remove road blocks

label: Treats me with respect
definition: Treats the decision-maker as competent; not arrogant or condescending. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: − : arrogant; treated as if I don't know; knows everything better; pretentious
example: arrogant company owner that knows everything better

label: A stable, established vendor
definition: The vendor is established and likely to be around; − : company status questionable. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: established companies; reputation; − : may fold or be sold

label: Proven track record
definition: Evidence of past success: experience, references, a record on similar problems. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: track record; experience; references
example: Track record on similar challenge elsewhere

label: Fits our environment
definition: The offering fits or integrates with the customer's environment and needs. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: integrates; fits my needs; feasibility in our environment; − : inadequate solutions
example: The ability to link a product that can be integrated in our specific IT environment.

label: Easy to deal with
definition: Simple and efficient to work with; − : complex, cumbersome, hard to pin down, badly organised. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: easy; efficient; − : too complex, cumbersome, endless discussions

label: Personal attention
definition: Personal, human attention and rapport. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: personal conversations; charisma; personalised; − : not personal enough, only technocrats

label: Committed to us
definition: Gives the customer priority, time and effort. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: stays close to our business; dedicated; always coming to see us; − : too busy, not dedicated, unwilling to travel

label: Competent people
definition: The people are capable at their job (general competence). Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: good sales reps; knowledgeable; − : useless, poor quality manager, not sufficient competence
exclude: product knowledge (B-PRODUCT-EXPERTISE); knowledge of my business (B-KNOWS-BUSINESS)

label: Support after the sale
definition: Service and support when the product is in use. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: customer service; customer support; − : poor deployment support, denies there is a problem

label: Partners with us
definition: Works with the customer as a partner, not a seller. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: partnership; works with us; extension of our business; − : body shop, not a strategic partner

label: Helps me sell it internally
definition: Helps the decision-maker carry the idea inside their own company. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: helps sell internally; helps me make the case to upper management
example: KAM: understands how my company works and helps sell internally
source: M2/M4 (inductive — answers lexicon gap L17 in the decision-maker's words); example Q24-R245

label: Quantifies the value
definition: Shows the return on investment or quantified impact. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: ROI; quantified; − : cannot quantify

label: Keeps promises; delivers
definition: Delivers what was promised; keeps commitments; what is delivered matches what was sold. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: keeps commitments; does what they say; delivers; − : over-promised, hype vs delivery
example: Genpact since they don't keep commitments

label: Solves my problem
definition: Helps the decision-maker solve a problem or reach a result; consultative. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: solutions; helps us; problem solving; advice; consultative
example: Understands my needs and knows how to help me.
source: M4 seed; Q11_1; lexicon L14; example Q24-R197

label: Continuity and long relationship
definition: A relationship built over time with the same people; − : turnover, inconsistency, no relationship. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: known them for years; long-term; same contact
example: IBM ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE HAVE KNOWN FOR 8 YEARS
source: M4 seed; lexicon L25; example Q24-R292

label: Communicates clearly
definition: Clear, relevant communication. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: clear; to the point; explains well

label: Flexible
definition: Adapts offering, terms or approach to the customer. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: flexible; customised; willing to adapt
example: CEO => very flexible in all matters

label: Price and value for money
definition: Price, cost, or value for money. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: price; cost; cheap; expensive; value for money
source: M4 seed; lexicon L20; example Q15_Other-R357

label: Product quality
definition: Quality or performance of what is sold. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: quality; reliability of product; innovation; best product

label: Professional
definition: Professional conduct and image. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
include: professional; courteous; polite
